method: Each run completes with exit code 0 and produces 5 samples for each of 3 workloads and 4 phases.
Each sample creates a fresh database under the system temporary directory and reopens it before reads.
The tree phase runs first, then indexed reads, then append; read phases share the reopened database cache.
Preparation is outside the timed commit. Commit includes its existing metadata and payload verification.
Trees and reads are checked against ordered expected chunk hashes and sizes; committed revision verification also runs after every sample.
Allocation measurements count requested allocation/reallocation bytes; they are allocation traffic, not live/peak RSS or filesystem I/O.
The append destination is preallocated outside its measured phase; indexed reads retain their owned results.
The unique 16 MiB file has a distinct 8-byte prefix per fixed 256 KiB chunk; the repeated file contains one repeated chunk.
The directory workload has 2048 ordered files, each 64 bytes with a distinct 8-byte prefix.
No network or competing transfer implementation is measured. These results do not establish end-to-end transfer speed.
The initial candidate and baseline-repeat bracket the candidate measurement; candidate-final repeats the measurement after final formatting and validation.
